wikipedia: State of Slovenes, Croats and Serbs

predecessors.name: Austria-Hungary
predecessors.text: the South Slav lands of Austria-Hungary (Croatia-Slavonia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Dalmatia, Carniola, Styria, Carinthia) without Istria, Prekmurje and Međimurje, with Syrmia

successors.name: Kingdom of Yugoslavia (Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes)
successors.text: the State of Slovenes, Croats and Serbs, joined to Serbia (without Istria, Prekmurje, Međimurje and Syrmia)

successors.name: Kingdom of Italy
successors.text: Istria, which the page calls disputed, 'officially ceded to Italy by the Treaty of Rapallo' and occupied by Italy after the armistice

ledger.x: 29 October 1918: the State of Slovenes, Croats and Serbs is proclaimed at Zagreb.
4 November 1918: Italy occupies the Adriatic coast.
November 1918: the State's units fight for Međimurje.
24 November 1918: Syrmia secedes and joins Serbia.
ledger.cpn: Serbia (Revolutionary Serbia, Principality and Kingdom of Serbia)

ledger.x: A bridge at the state's end (1 December 1918): the contest passes to the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes.
1 December 1918: this record closes with the state, not with the occupation.
1 December 1918: the state joins Serbia in the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes.
ledger.cpn: Kingdom of Yugoslavia (Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes)

wars.name: Italian occupation of the Adriatic coast after the Armistice of Villa Giusti
wars.outcome: Italy occupied Istria and much of Dalmatia under the armistice of 3-4 November 1918 and stayed until 1921; the Treaty of Rapallo ceded Istria to Italy.

wars.name: Međimurje clash with the Hungarian garrison, November 1918
wars.outcome: The State's units engaged the Hungarian garrison in November 1918; the first attempt was defeated at Čakovec and a second, under Slavko Kvaternik, forced the Hungarian troops out (month not given); Međimurje joined the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes on…

certainty.note: The state was an unrecognised provisional government; no page gives its frontier, and the Adriatic, Carinthian, Syrmian and Međimurje frontiers were all in dispute.
